name: Acquired Cystic Disease-Associated Renal Cell Carcinoma
aliases: Acquired cystic kidney disease-related renal cell carcinoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Urinary System and Male Genital Organs

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic histological features including eosinophilic cytoplasm with prominent nucleoli and frequent intratumoral oxalate crystals
History of end-stage renal disease with acquired cystic kidney disease
Renal imaging showing multiple acquired cysts with a solid enhancing renal mass
Positive staining for AMACR (alpha-methylacyl-CoA racemase) and CK7 variable expression

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of characteristic tumor features in a patient with acquired cystic kidney disease and compatible imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires correlation of clinical history, imaging, and histopathology; immunohistochemistry supports but is not definitive alone.

pathognomonic.notes: Often detected late due to tumor growth
Visible blood in urine due to tumor bleeding

common.symptomName: Flank pain localized to affected kidney
common.notes: Due to tumor mass effect or hemorrhage
Secondary to chronic blood loss or renal dysfunction
searchTerms: fatigue related to low red blood cells

common.notes: May be secondary to renal impairment

occasional.notes: Related to chronic inflammation and renal failure
searchTerms: low red blood cells from chronic illness
chronic disease causing low blood count

rare.symptomName: Metastatic symptoms such as bone pain
searchTerms: pain in bones due to metastasis
symptoms from cancer spread to bones

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine consistent with renal impairment
imaging: Ultrasound or CT showing multiple acquired renal cysts with a solid enhancing mass
MRI demonstrating tumor characteristics and local invasion
genetic: No consistent germline mutations identified; somatic mutations may include chromosomal losses typical of RCC
other: Histopathology revealing eosinophilic cells with prominent nucleoli and intratumoral oxalate crystals

distinguishingFeatures: Clear cytoplasm on histology versus eosinophilic cytoplasm in ACD-associated RCC
Frequent trisomy of chromosomes 7 and 17, absent in ACD-associated RCC
Benign tumor with uniform eosinophilic cells lacking malignant features

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging renal mass in a patient with acquired cystic kidney disease
Signs of metastatic spread such as bone pain or weight loss
references: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Urinary System and Male Genital Organs, 5th Edition, 2022
Tickoo SK, et al. Acquired cystic disease-associated renal cell carcinoma: a distinct entity with unique morphology and immunohistochemical profile. Am J Surg Pathol. 2006
Orphanet: Acquired cystic disease-associated renal cell carcinoma (ORPHA:404514)
